**Claimed and dispatched by the PM loop.**

- Session: `session_01HDA9nN6nXQngoQUAAzRdMb`
- Branch: `claude/issue-5296-changesets-v3`
- Worktree: `../objectui-issue-5296` (dedicated, per repo — no edits in the shared checkout, no `git stash`)
- Model: `opus`. The contract-review tier (`claude-fable-5`) was measured unavailable twice today on quota; the 2026-08-13 exemption ("fable 用完了可以用 opus") applies, and this card is a config migration with a rehearsal, not a contract review.

Routing authority, verbatim from the maintainer: **"按照你的建议派发执行"** — i.e. file the card and dispatch it, which is what this comment records.

## File territory this claim covers

`package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.changeset/config.json`, `scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `.github/workflows/changeset-release.yml` (last one only if item 4 in the body measures a real change), plus one `.changeset/*.md`.

Nothing else. In particular this claim does **not** cover `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`, the `changesets/action@v1` pin, or any of the 250 pending changeset files.

## Serial constraints handed to the dev seat

1. **One PR.** The bump and the config changes land together or not at all — split, each half is silently wrong until the next release.
2. **Rehearse in a throwaway clone with its remote removed.** Never `origin`, never a pushable worktree.
3. **Perform no release.** No `changeset publish`, no version tag, no release-workflow dispatch, no merging of a Version Packages PR.
4. **Measure, do not reason**, for the `changeset version`-on-empty-plan question — the answer goes in the PR body either way.
5. **The gate scripts' self-tests must model v3.** A self-test that still asserts v2 semantics and passes is a failed run.

Dependabot #4950 stays open and unmerged until `main` carries `^3.0.0`, at which point it closes itself.

**Correction to this card's body — a measurement I published here is wrong.**

The body states, under item 1: *"Across the current 250 pending changesets, **none names it**, so the trap does not fire today."* That is false. Verified independently against `origin/main` (`7260a1ed4`), not against the dev seat's report: `.changeset/no-console-lint-rule.md` names the private `object-ui` beside four published packages —

```
'@object-ui/app-shell': patch
'@object-ui/fields': patch
'@object-ui/plugin-detail': patch
'@object-ui/runner': patch
'object-ui': patch
```

So under v3 with `privatePackages` left undeclared, that is a mixed changeset and `changeset status` exits 1 **on today's stock**, not on some future one.

Why I got it wrong: the private package's name is `object-ui`, which is a substring of all 40 `@object-ui/*` scoped names in those same files. Any unanchored search over `.changeset/` either matches every file or, once filtered, hides the one line that matters. The check had to be anchored — `^'object-ui':` — and I did not anchor it. One grep away, and I reported the loose result as a measurement.

The correction **strengthens** the card rather than weakening it. The body's argument was "the trap does not fire today, but 'not today' is not a plan, so set the key explicitly." The real position is worse: dependabot's #4950, merged as it stands, would have stopped the release lane on the very next push to `main` — with PR CI green, because no PR workflow in this repo runs `changeset status`. The reason for the card holds; the margin I claimed did not exist.

Found by the dev seat during rehearsal, which is where it should have been found — and it is on record here because a card body that stays wrong is worse than one that is visibly corrected.

## Measurements per the four items

1. **`privatePackages`** — default flips from `{version:true, tag:false}` (v2) to `{version:false, tag:false}` (v3), read out of `@changesets/config@4.0.0`; `version:false` feeds `allowPrivatePackages:false` into the assembler, i.e. private packages become *ignored*. Three settings rehearsed on the real stock: absent → exit 1 mixed changeset; `{version:false,tag:false}` → exit 1 mixed changeset; `{version:true,tag:false}` → exit 0 with a plan identical to v2. `tag:false` verified as the right half too — `getPublishPlan.mjs` filters private packages out of the npm publish set unconditionally, so only tagging is at stake. Moving `object-ui` to `ignore` was rejected: `check-changeset-presence.mjs` derives its guarded surface from `fixed`, so that would silently stop demanding changesets for the extension's source.
2. **Experimental key** — `@changesets/assemble-release-plan@6.0.10` references `onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange` 6 times in its dist, `@7.0.0` references it 0 times: load-bearing under v2, inert under v3. `@changesets/config@4.0.0` still parses it, so it would have been accepted-and-dead. A v3 run with the key re-added produced a byte-identical plan.
3. **Engines** — `^22.11 || ^24 || >=26`, `"type": "module"`. Repo pin does **not** satisfy it; nothing enforces it today. Reported, not changed → #5306.
4. **`changeset version` on an empty plan** — the exit-code change is real (v2: exit 0 `warn No unreleased changesets found, exiting.`; v3: exit **1** `No unreleased changesets found.`), but a stock of only empty-frontmatter changesets exits 0 under **both**. And it is unreachable through this workflow: `changesets/action@v1` resolves to v1.9.0, whose `src/index.ts` and compiled `dist/index.js` return via `runPublish` when there are no changesets and via `"All changesets are empty; not creating PR"` when all are empty — `runVersion` is reached only when at least one changeset carries a release. The action reads changesets with its own bundled `@changesets/*`, so this bump cannot change which branch it takes. **No workflow change.**

## Non-goals honoured

No release performed (no `changeset publish`, no tag, no workflow dispatch, no version PR merged); pre mode not entered; `changesets/action@v1` pin read but untouched; `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` and all 249 pre-existing changeset files untouched; #4950 left open and unmerged; no label minted.

## Beyond the claimed file territory (one file)

`scripts/__tests__/check-changeset-fixed.test.ts` is new. The card asks for both gate scripts' self-tests to pass and model v3 — `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` had **no self-test at all** (only `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-changeset-presence` have one), so that criterion could not otherwise be met. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` needed no change: it hand-parses frontmatter and must not import `@changesets/*` (it runs on a bare checkout), so nothing in it models v2.

**Landed.** PR #5307 went through the merge queue at 08:43 and is on `main`.

Verified by **content on `origin/main`** (`e7c3b3e91`), not by sha ancestry — the queue lands as a squash, so ancestry would prove nothing:

- `package.json` → `"@changesets/cli": "^3.0.0"`
- `.changeset/config.json` → `$schema` at `@changesets/config@4.0.0`, `privatePackages: { "version": true, "tag": false }` present, `___experimentalUnsafeOptions_WILL_CHANGE_IN_PATCH` gone

All four items in this card's body are answered on the PR, one of them by correcting the card: the mixed-changeset trap was live on today's stock, not hypothetical. Item 4 came back "no real change" — `changeset-release.yml` is untouched, with the pinned action's branch logic as the reason.

Two things this does **not** yet establish, and I am not claiming them:

1. **Dependabot #4950 has not closed itself yet.** It was still open on the read after the merge. It should retire on dependabot's next run now that `main` carries `^3.0.0`; if it doesn't, that gets chased rather than merged by hand.
2. **The release lane has not run under v3 yet.** `changeset-release.yml` is the only place `changeset version` is ever invoked, so the push to `main` is the first real exercise of this migration. Being watched; a failure there is a direct consequence of this change, not an unrelated event.

Split out rather than ridden in: #5306 (root `engines` looser than the toolchain now requires).

**Close-out — both items I left open above are now settled, and the migration is proven on the release lane rather than only in rehearsal.**

**1. Dependabot #4950 retired itself.** Closed `2026-08-19T08:46:02Z`, three minutes after #5307 landed, and its branch is gone. Checked two ways (PR state, and `git ls-remote` for `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/changesets/cli-3.0.0`). My note above said it had not closed yet — that was true when written; no intervention was needed.

**2. `changeset-release.yml` ran green under v3.** Run [`32234037039`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32234037039) on `e7c3b3e91`, all steps success, including step 11 *Create Release Pull Request or Publish to npm*.

This is the part rehearsal could not prove, so it is worth stating what the live lane actually did. The action took the `hasChangesets → runVersion` branch — it **updated the existing version PR #4655** (touched at 09:12:57, the second step 11 finished) and did **not** publish, which is exactly the branch behaviour the PR body argued from `changesets/action@v1.9.0`'s source. Read off `origin/changeset-release/main` (`8715f50`):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `object-ui` (private, `packages/vscode-extension`) | `17.6.0`, still `"private": true` |
| `@object-ui/types` (published) | `17.6.0` |
| `.changeset/` contents | only `README.md` + `config.json` — all 249 consumed |

The private extension bumping **in lockstep** is the whole point of `privatePackages: { "version": true, "tag": false }`. Had the key been left undeclared — i.e. had #4950 been merged as it stood — this run would have failed with `Found mixed changeset no-console-lint-rule` instead, and it would have been the first anyone heard of it. The rehearsal's prediction (40 packages `17.5.0 → 17.6.0`, 249 changesets consumed, `README.md` kept) matches the live output exactly.

**No release was performed and none will be from this lane by an agent.** Version PR #4655 is open and now regenerated under v3; merging it *is* the release, and that is the maintainer's call, not this loop's. It is reported here, not touched.

Card complete. Split out and still open: #5306 (root `engines` looser than the toolchain now requires).
